result.title: Potential Games for Self-Neighborhood Channel Mixing in Graph Neural Networks
result.summary: Graph message passing must balance two competing objectives: incorporating neighborhood signals while preserving node-specific information. We model this trade-off as a game in which nodes choose how to mix their own representations with strict-neighborhood aggregates. For fixed channel representations, task supervision defines a common-payoff game, while local distinctness payoffs induce an exact potential game whose potential is the degree-normalized strict Dirichlet energy. We introduce CG2, which amortizes these choices through a shared six-parameter policy per layer based on local channel statistics and can be trained using either objective. Controlled comparisons show that the shared task-trained policy improves mean performance over fixed mixing on three of five heterophily benchmarks, with significant gains on two, while free per-node actions trained with either objective rarely improve on the same baseline. On the ECHO long-range benchmark, the clearest contribution of the gate appears on eccentricity, where the task-trained policy substantially reduces prediction error.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将图消息传递中「吸收邻域信号」与「保留节点自身信息」的权衡建模为势博弈（势函数为度归一化的严格 Dirichlet 能量），并提出 CG2：每层用基于局部通道统计的共享六参数策略自适应决定自身表示与邻域聚合的混合比例，可按任务监督或该能量目标训练，在异质图与长程基准上与固定混合对比。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按局部统计决定「吸收多少外部信息、保留多少自身状态」的轻量共享门控，以及用能量项抑制表示过度平滑的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态更新与表示坍缩、区分度监督的设计。
